s: Today we are talking about school life, because today's five words are all about learning: teacher, student, lesson, homework, and exam.
And I want to start with the word teacher.
A teacher is a person who helps you learn at school.
Oh, I remember my first English teacher!
A good teacher makes every lesson easy to understand.
My teacher always smiled and said hello to each student.
And when a teacher explains things slowly, every student can follow the lesson.
My teacher used funny stories, and the whole class laughed.
Now, the second word is student.
A student is a person who learns at school or in a class.
Are you a student, or do you know a student?
I was a student for many years!
Every student needs a good teacher.
And when the student does the homework, the teacher is happy.
A student also needs good friends at school.
My best friend was a student in my class, and we did our homework together after every lesson.
So our third word is lesson.
A lesson is one short class, one time of learning.
We have a new English lesson every morning here on Word Kitchen.
In one lesson, the teacher shows new words.
After the lesson, there is homework!
A lesson can be thirty minutes or one hour.
I like a lesson that starts with a song.
It helps every student relax before the hard work.
Homework is school work you do at home.
I finish my homework after dinner.
I always did my homework at the kitchen table.
When the teacher gives homework, the student must do it before the next lesson.
And homework helps you remember the lesson.
If the student skips the homework, the exam becomes very hard!
An exam is a test at school.
We have a big exam on Friday.
Exams can be scary, but they are not bad.
An exam shows the teacher what each student learned.
After the exam, the student knows what to study next.
To do well on an exam, the student should listen in every lesson and finish the homework every day.
A good teacher helps the student feel ready for the exam.
Let's review our five words one more time.
A teacher is the person who teaches you.
A student is the person who learns.
Homework is the work you do at home.
And an exam is a test at school.
Now, let me ask you, Lena.
Did you like your teacher at school?
My teacher was funny and kind.
I was a student who loved books.
I did my homework on time, but I was always nervous before an exam.
Before an exam, I studied all evening.
I read my notes after dinner, and I asked my teacher for help when I did not understand the lesson.
A smart student asks the teacher questions.
And a kind teacher always answers.
That's how the student grows lesson by lesson.
Wait, Maya, can I ask you something?
What is the difference between a lesson and homework?
A lesson happens at school with the teacher.
Homework happens at home, after the lesson.
So in the lesson, the student learns new things.
And with homework, the student practices at home?
The teacher teaches the lesson, and the student does the homework.
Both help the student get ready for the exam.
I love that: lesson by lesson.
So, dear listeners, use these words today.
Think about one student you know.
And don't be afraid of the next exam.
Every exam is a chance to show what you learned.
Thanks for listening to Word Kitchen!
